headline: Siri AI shows 'very good' results after one week of testing
summary: A week-long test of iOS 27's new Siri AI reveals impressive capabilities, offering proactive assistance and detailed information.
details: Joanna Stern from 9to5Mac spent seven days rigorously testing the upcoming AI-powered Siri, integrated into iOS 27.
The AI demonstrated a strong ability to understand context and provide useful, proactive suggestions based on the user's schedule and communications.
For example, Siri alerted the user to a potential delay for an upcoming appearance due to traffic and reminded them of a voicemail from a book group.
Stern's review suggests that this new iteration of Siri is a significant improvement, moving beyond simple command execution to more intelligent assistance.
caption:
Apple's new Siri AI has been tested for a week, and early results are 'very good'.

Joanna Stern from 9to5Mac spent seven days rigorously testing the upcoming AI-powered Siri, integrated into iOS 27.

The AI demonstrated a strong ability to understand context and provide useful, proactive suggestions based on the user's schedule and communications.

For example, Siri alerted the user to a potential delay for an upcoming appearance due to traffic and reminded them of a voicemail from a book group.

Stern's review suggests that this new iteration of Siri is a significant improvement, moving beyond simple command execution to more intelligent assistance.

topic: industry giants crack 2d transistor scaling bottleneck
headline_marked: [[2D Transistor Scaling]] Breakthrough Achieved by imec, ASML, and TSMC
headline: 2D Transistor Scaling Breakthrough Achieved by imec, ASML, and TSMC
summary: Industry giants have successfully integrated complementary 2D-material transistors at a 50nm pitch, a critical step towards the post-silicon era.
details: Imec, ASML, and TSMC have achieved a significant milestone by integrating both n-type and p-type transistors with atomically thin 2D channels on a single 300mm wafer. This breakthrough technology demonstrates a 50nm contacted poly pitch, the tightest yet for complementary 2D devices, bringing us closer to the post-silicon era.

The collaboration utilized a single EUV exposure to print channel lengths as short as 28nm. Imec reported that an impressive 94% of the integrated transistors switched correctly, boasting an on/off current ratio exceeding 100,000, showcasing the viability of this advanced manufacturing process.

This advancement moves beyond isolated single devices, integrating complementary polarities on a standard 300mm process flow. The n-channel devices use molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), while the p-channel devices employ tungsten diselenide (WSe2) or tungsten disulfide (WS2), demonstrating the versatility of 2D materials in next-generation chips.

A key innovation involved inverting the usual build order, patterning tungsten-filled contact trenches first and then transferring the 2D channel on top. This 'reverse' thin-film-transistor flow resulted in clean off-state behavior, with both polarities effectively shutting off at zero gate voltage, a crucial factor for low-power computing.

The demonstrated transistors achieved active widths down to 75nm and an equivalent oxide thickness near 2nm. The performance of the WSe2 p-channel devices now rivals the best lab-scale results, significantly narrowing the gap on the historically weaker p-type side of 2D CMOS technology.

This 50nm pitch is tighter than that of Intel's 10nm-class node, indicating that 2D transistors are scaling effectively. The use of standard EUV lithography, rather than more complex High-NA tooling, further suggests a more accessible path to mass production for these advanced components.
